# SPE Round r01 Plan: Triage Agent

The spec is your prompt: "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." Nothing exists yet. This round builds the triage agent, a labeled ticket set, and a grader. Then it measures three configurations against the predictions below. All commits stay local. Nothing gets pushed.

## 1. Specify

### Defaults I chose (logged in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Default | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | There are no real tickets, so I will write 60 synthetic support tickets. Each of the 6 categories gets 10 tickets. 12 of the 60 are hard cases with ambiguous wording, more than one issue, or misleading keywords. | User. Please supply real tickets for r02. |
| D2 | Labels are category plus priority. The categories are `billing`, `bug`, `account_access`, `feature_request`, `outage`, and `other`. The priorities are `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, and `P4`. | User |
| D3 | "Correctly" means category accuracy of at least 90%, priority accuracy of at least 80%, and P1 recall of at least 95%. | User |
| D4 | "Cheaply" means at most $3.00 per 1,000 tickets in model API cost. | User |
| D5 | The agent is Python on the Anthropic SDK. It reads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the environment and never prints it. | Logged default |
| D6 | Config C tests a smaller model because the spec says "cheaply." I will confirm current model IDs and prices from the docs before the harness runs. | User. You can reject C, and I will drop it. |
| D7 | Every requirement can be checked by code, so r01 uses no LLM judge. | Logged default |
| D8 | A second Opus subagent labels all 60 tickets blind. Any ticket where its label differs from mine is left out of scoring. I log the count and list those tickets for you to rule on. | Logged default |

### Requirement table (`spe/spec/spec.md`, round r01)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Category exact match on at least 90% of scored tickets | "triage tickets correctly", D3 | `check_category_exact` |
| R2 | Priority exact match on at least 80% of scored tickets | "triage tickets correctly", D3 | `check_priority_exact` |
| R3 | At least 95% of gold P1 tickets are labeled P1 | "correctly", D3 | `check_p1_recall` |
| R4 | 100% of outputs are valid JSON that matches `triage/schema.json` | Decision | `check_schema` |
| R5 | Cost of at most $3.00 per 1,000 tickets, computed from logged token usage and current prices | "cheaply", D4 | `cost_from_usage` |
| R6 | At least 90% of tickets get the same category and priority on all 3 repeats | Decision | `check_repeat_agreement` |
| R7 | The prompts and few-shot examples contain no eval ticket text | Decision | `check_no_overlap` (pre-launch gate) |

r01 is the first round, so there are no proposals from an earlier round to adopt or reject.

## 2. Predict

### Configurations

Each config changes one thing from A.

| Config | Model | Prompt | Changed from A |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Sonnet (current) | `triage/prompts/base.md`, zero-shot | Baseline |
| B | Sonnet (current) | Base plus 6 few-shot examples from `triage/prompts/fewshot.md` | Adds few-shot examples |
| C | Haiku (current) | `triage/prompts/base.md`, zero-shot | Uses a smaller model |

### Predicted numbers (saved to `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`)

| Metric | A | B | C | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy | 88% | 92% | 82% | `check_category_exact` | The hard cases cost about 7 points. Examples recover about 4 of them. A smaller model loses about 6 more. |
| Priority accuracy | 72% | 78% | 65% | `check_priority_exact` | The line between P2 and P3 is fuzzy without a rubric. Examples show where the line sits. |
| P1 recall | 90% | 92% | 85% | `check_p1_recall` | Outages are easy to spot. P1 tickets that read like bugs get marked P2. |
| Schema valid | 100% | 100% | 99% | `check_schema` | Structured output enforces the schema. A smaller model may truncate one output. |
| Cost per 1,000 tickets (USD) | $2.55 | $5.25 | $0.85 | `cost_from_usage` | Each call is about 550 input and 60 output tokens. The examples add about 900 input tokens. Prices are estimates until I confirm them. |
| Repeat agreement | 93% | 95% | 90% | `check_repeat_agreement` | Hard cases flip between runs. Examples anchor them. |

**Predicted outcome:** no config passes everything. A just misses R1 and R2. B passes R1 but fails R2 and R5. C passes R5 but fails R1, R2, and R3. Every config fails R2 at 80%. I expect that a priority rubric, not a model change, is the r02 fix.

**Naive guess for comparison:** all three configs score the same as A on every quality metric. At close-out I will say plainly whether this guess was closer than mine.

**Trivial baseline:** labeling every ticket with the majority class scores about 17% category accuracy. This is the control in Gate 2.

`same_as_last_round` is `null` for every number because no earlier round exists.

## 3. Evaluate

### Build steps (before the Workflow)

1. Create `triage/agent.py`, `triage/run.py`, `triage/schema.json`, `triage/prompts/base.md`, and `triage/prompts/fewshot.md`. The output schema has 4 fields: `category`, `priority`, `reason`, and `ticket_id`.
2. Create `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` (ticket text only) and `spe/evals/data/answers.jsonl` (gold labels). The few-shot examples come from a separate set of 6 tickets that are not in the eval set.
3. Create `spe/evals/graders/grade.py` and `spe/evals/graders/selftest.py`.
4. Create `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js` with `const ROUND = "r01"`. Every prompt string reads the round from that constant.

### Gates before launch

| Gate | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| G1 Grader selftest | Oracle predictions copied from `answers.jsonl` score 100% on R1 to R4. Empty outputs fail R4 and score 0 on R1. Shifted wrong labels score 0 on R1. |
| G2 Control | No last round exists to regrade. The majority-class baseline regrades to about 17% on R1 instead. |
| G3 Overlap | `check_no_overlap` finds no eval ticket text in either prompt file. |
| G4 Label agreement | The blind second labeling runs. I report the excluded count. If more than 6 tickets are excluded, I halt and ask you. |
| G5 Dry run | 3 cells run end to end and get graded: A × T01, B × T25, C × T48. |

Any failed gate halts the round and gets reported.

### Workflow run

- A cell is one config and one ticket. A trial is one run of a cell. There are 3 configs × 60 tickets × 3 repeats = 540 base trials.
- Trial steps call `python -I triage/run.py --config <X> --ticket <ID>` directly. The triage agent has no file or tool access. It sees only its prompt and the ticket text.
- Each trial returns the output schema plus token usage, which is logged to `spe/evals/results/r01/trials.jsonl`.
- Code grading runs after all trials finish. Trials never read `answers.jsonl`, the graders, or `spe/predictions/`.
- Peek scan: every logged request is scanned for strings from `answers.jsonl` and the predictions file. I void any trial that matches and log it.
- Split cells: if a cell's 3 repeats disagree, it gets up to 2 more trials, capped at 5 trials per cell.
- Caps: $10.00 of API spend and 900 API calls. A trial that would cross either cap is skipped and logged in `spe/evals/results/r01/skips.md`.
- Failure analysis: an Opus subagent groups the wrong cells into F-numbered failure types.
- Completeness critic: an Opus subagent checks that every predicted cell has a measured number and that every void and skip is logged.

### Workflow arguments

```json
{
  "ROUND": "r01",
  "configs": ["A", "B", "C"],
  "tickets": "spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl",
  "repeats": 3,
  "extra_trials_per_split_cell": 2,
  "max_trials_per_cell": 5,
  "budget_usd": 10.00,
  "max_api_calls": 900,
  "subagent_model": "opus"
}
```

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

- Base trials: about $0.46 for A, $0.95 for B, and $0.15 for C. That is about $1.56 in total.
- Extra trials and dry run: up to about $0.60.
- Opus subagents for ticket writing, blind labeling, failure analysis, and the critic: about 4 runs. This is the largest cost, and I cannot estimate it well before measuring.
- Wall time: about 20 to 30 minutes.

## 4. After approval, before anything else

1. Save your prompt and planning answers verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md`. Write `spe/spec/spec.md` and `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Commit as `SPE r01 specify`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. Its first line is `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It records round, date, author ("Claude, approved by the user in plan mode"), configs, every number with its Why, and `same_as_last_round: null`. Commit as `SPE r01 predict: A/B/C baseline, few-shot, smaller model`.
3. Build the agent, data, graders, and harness. Run gates G1 to G5. Commit as `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)`.
4. Launch the Workflow. When its completion notice arrives, commit the results as `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>`.

## 5. Close-out (learn)

- `spe/prediction-log.md` gets one row per metric and config with these columns: Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, Closer. Below the table, "Which Why broke" quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. I also state whether the naive guess beat my predictions.
- `spe/failures.md` gets an entry for each new failure type with Name, Kind, Round, What, How to spot it, Seen in, and Fix. A grader bug found after the run counts as a failure. Original and regraded numbers sit side by side.
- `spe/spec/spec.md` gets a "Proposed for round r02" table. `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` is written with `status: draft`.
- `spe/README.md` is updated. Then I commit `SPE r01 learn: <headline>` and tag `spe-r01`.

## 6. Halt and stop rules

- I halt and report if the budget cap is hit, an answer key leaks into a trial, a grader is broken, or a decision only you can make comes up.
- If every config passes everything, r02 needs harder tickets or stricter graders.
- The loop stops when predictions match results for 3 rounds in a row.
- I will not push, deploy, or send anything.
critiques: The plan quotes the prompt "triage tickets correctly and cheaply" as the spec. It then builds a requirement table R1 to R7. Each row has a Source tied to the prompt or a logged decision and a named Test, such as `check_category_exact` and `cost_from_usage`.

The predicted numbers table gives A, B, and C specific values for every metric. Examples are category accuracy of 88%, 92%, and 82%, and cost of $2.55, $5.25, and $0.85 per 1,000 tickets. It uses no adjectives in place of numbers.

Every metric row has a Why column that explains the numbers for all three configs. One example is "The hard cases cost about 7 points. Examples recover about 4 of them. A smaller model loses about 6 more." The cost row states its token assumptions.
